headline: Ireland fines Google roughly €400 million over location data practices
summary: Ireland's Data Protection Commission fined Google roughly €400 million for how it processed users' location data. Outlets report slightly different currency figures for the fine.

claims.statement: Ireland's Data Protection Commission fined Google roughly €400 million over its handling of users' location data.

sources.quote: Ireland's Data Protection Commission (DPC) has fined Google €403 million ($463M) for multiple GDPR violations related to processing users' location data.
Google fined more than €400m by Irish regulator over its use of location data
Google fined $463 million for breaching EU location data rules

discrepancies.explanation: Outlets report different currency figures for the fine: theguardian cites €400m/£345m, while engadget and bleepingcomputer cite $463 million (€403 million).

quotes.quote: Google has been fined more than €400m (£345m)
